page.layout: One printed page. Main text in one wide column. A narrow column of short hyphenated fragments stands in the left margin beside the text, so it is treated as left-margin notes. A short "Auena," line also sits in the left margin at the foot. Running head and page number at the top.

main_text.p: sefami genus est, quod ipsa ratio & descriptio indicat, excepto quod Ægyptiacum efficacius est & candidius. Hoc nostrum sesamum ab omnibus anulla tanquam inutile reiicitur, cum tamen ipsum emollire & calfacere, planiam [?] vero ò viridum vino decoctum inflammationem dolorésq, oculorum certò sedare experimentum sit. Quin & pani commixtum jucundum & dulce et aporem conciliat: per se vero ù usu patum stomacho non admodum confert, est enim oleosum & pingue, unde pingue alimentum praestat, craffum [?].

ex sefa-Placentae [?] fuccum. Cum melle crudo placentas ex eo confi-mo pu-ciebant, quas [?] vocabant. Apud Athe-bis mu-nem lib.14. huiusmodi placentas finguntur ex melle & sesamo torrefactis addito oleo: liebrismeminit praeterea & aliarum, quas ab uni-formamue sa Sicilia [illegible, ~6 letters] appellatas afferit, quae ex sesamo & melle mulieribus pubis formam fingebantur, repre-has enim feminae Dearum altaribus cir-sentan-tes.cumferebant.

Auena,Ad hanc haud penitendum f[?]umenti genus est. In [?] infulis quibusdam fola auena homines vi-vere memoriae productum est, utpote effonte [?] proeuenientes. Mos [?] fcrip ut Matthias Michon, aenam fublimant, ex qua sublima-tione elicitur liquor, quem aquam ardentem vi-tae vocant, ut apud Germanos, Italos, Gallos, ex vinis vehementioribus, bancq; summo eos habere pretio testantur, quibus legatione functi ut ii [?] redierunt domum. Quidam ex eis lenitor [?]
[Footnote lines at the foot not clearly legible; see notes.]

page.notes: Several words in the Greek and Latin text are not clearly legible at this scan resolution and are marked [?] or [illegible]. The Greek words "πλακοῦντας" and the Greek term after "Sicilia" are doubtful; they are not confidently read. The left column fragments are hyphenated pieces of running text set in the left margin. The catchword "lenitor" at the right foot is uncertain. The first line of the page is a continuation from the previous page. The printed footer note at the foot is not clearly readable and should be checked against the scan.
